chunks: Those among the Jews who distort the words from their contexts and say, 'We have heard and disobeyed,' and, 'Hear without hearing,' and, 'Listen to us,' twisting their tongues and reviling the faith. But if they had said, 'We have heard and obeyed,' and, 'Hear and regard us,' it would have been better for them and more appropriate. But God has disgraced them for their lack of belief; and so only a few of them believe.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Sami'na wa 'Adhna' and how did the Jews distort it?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the Jewish practice of linguistic distortion (ta'wil) where 'Sami'na' (We heard) was altered to 'Sami'na wa 'Adhna' (We heard and disobeyed) and 'Ra'ina' to 'La'ina' (Our fool), serving as a rhetorical critique of their superficial compliance. In Shia exegesis, this is often contrasted with the ideal of 'Sami'na wa 'Ata'na' (We heard and obeyed), emphasizing that true faith requires internalizing the command rather than merely uttering it. The verse concludes that despite the clarity of the message, their stubborn disbelief prevented most from accepting the truth.
